prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1343; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the right lane of a multi-lane roadway in Baytown, Texas, when Driver 1 moved left to change lanes and made contact with the side of a vehicle operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported the crash to responding officers and stated having pain in the left knee after the impact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed by both drivers and by a responding witness as being inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Several bystanders and Driver 2 gave statements consistent with Driver 1's account of how the lane change and contact occurred. Photographs taken at the scene show damage along the left rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle and the right front side of Driver 2's vehicle, which is largely consistent with a sideswipe of this nature. Some older scratches were also noted on the same panel, and it is unclear whether these predate the collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy under review. The reported knee injury appears consistent with the type and force of impact described at the scene.
